title: Patient Financial Services Manual — Retroactive Coverage and Rebilling of Posted Charges
content:
**2.1 Rule.** When a patient reports coverage that was already in force on the date of service of a charge that was posted as self-pay, or as patient responsibility under a different payer, the group rebills the claim to the newly reported payer and removes the charge from the patient's balance of the Patient Financial Account with one adjustment coded as a retroactive-coverage rebill. The adjustment equals the charge's remaining balance: the charge amount, less every time-of-service collection, payment and adjustment applied to that charge, plus the amount of any of those payments later reversed.

**2.2 Recording first.** The new coverage must first be recorded on the account by a coverage update.

**2.3 Coverage in force on the date of service.** The newly reported coverage's effective date on the account is on or before the date of service of the charge. The effective date is the one recorded on the account; the date of service is the one on the charge being rebilled.

**2.4 Filing limit.** The handling date is no later than the new tier's timely-filing limit counted from the date of service of the charge.

- The limit is counted in calendar days starting the day after the date of service, and a handling date that falls exactly on the last day of the limit still qualifies.
- The limit is the timely-filing figure of the tier the account holds after the coverage update.
- A tier whose timely-filing figure is 0 has no payer to rebill and never qualifies.

**2.5 One rebill per charge.** A charge already rebilled once is not rebilled again; the account ledger shows whether a retroactive-coverage rebill adjustment already sits on the charge.

**2.6 Outside the limit.** A charge outside the limit stays patient responsibility (a self-pay discount already applied to it stands), and the patient may pursue the insurer directly; the group does not refile late.

**2.7 Payments already made.** Payments already applied to a rebilled charge become a credit on the account, handled under the credit balance rules of the Patient Financial Account.

### Boundary illustration (hypothetical dates)

Take a date of service on day 0 and a new tier whose timely-filing limit is 90 days. Day 1 is the first counted day and day 90 is the last.

| Handling date | Within the limit? |
|---|---|
| day 89 | yes |
| day 90 (last day of the limit) | yes |
| day 91 | no — the charge stays patient responsibility |

### Condition checklist for one charge

| Condition | Source of the fact |
|---|---|
| new coverage recorded on the account by a coverage update | account record |
| recorded effective date on or before the charge's date of service | account record and charge |
| handling date within the new tier's filing limit, and that limit above 0 | charge date of service and the tier's figure |
| no earlier retroactive-coverage rebill on the charge | account ledger |
